status: Search bounds informed by geometry feasibility probes; not proven feasible for every combination.
architecture: slit -> added mirror F1 -> powered M1 -> curved reflective grating -> powered M2 -> added mirror F2 -> detector
first_experiment: CMA flat-fold control, inherited powered prescription fixed
conventions: Turn is angle between incoming and outgoing propagation directions, not incidence angle. Azimuth uses four_mirror._flat transverse frame. Fractions refer to inherited unfolded chief legs; splitting preserves leg length.

evidence.role: Preliminary differential-evolution/local-search feasibility probe, not a CMA result
Broader random geometry probe found full-support layouts with second fold fraction around .80, motivating expanded bounds

workflow: Three population CMA runs, 3600 evaluations each, population24; independent seeds and recorded restarts. No local refinement in this stage. Retain actual evaluated candidates, audit selected incumbents, and render feasible layouts.
limitations: Feasible examples do not establish feasibility of the full hyperrectangle.
Flat folds retain inherited optical aberrations.
Circular apertures sized from training rays; dense heldout checks are required.
Optical gap and envelope omit substrates, mounts, and detector housing.
